theorem_title: Every entry of a zero-sum natural-number list vanishes
natural_language_statement:
Let $L$ be a finite list of natural numbers whose sum is zero. Then

$$\sum_{g\in L}g=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\forall g\in L,\ g=0.$$

The sum counts repeated list entries. This elementary fact can finish a degree-telescoping argument once that argument has produced a zero sum of nonnegative degrees; no polynomial or cycle hypotheses are part of this theorem.
formal_statement:
theorem CollatzWork.Disproof.quotientDegreesVanish
    (degrees : List Nat)
    (hSum : degrees.sum = 0) :
    ∀ g ∈ degrees, g = 0 := by sorry
